title: GCP trust anchor pin removal is not revocation; partial federation failure leaves pinned-but-contextless anchor
description: Found in 3x codereview of w0fp. Two related semantics in the lichend GCP-3.1 flow: (1) TrustStore provisioning is monotonic (rust/lichen-gateway/src/trust.rs provision_configured_peer 672-713 only adds/raises level; TrustStore::remove 1067 has no daemon caller), so dropping a compromised peer key from gateway_coordination.peer_public_keys in deploy/lichend.toml.example does NOT revoke its durable BrProvisioned pin or GCP context — an explicit operator revocation path (config change -> pin+context removal, atomic with persistence) is missing. (2) provision_closed_federation (rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs:1039-1099) commits trust anchors durably (save_atomic_with_floor 1081-1090) before installing contexts (1091-1097); a context-install failure exits the daemon with the anchor pinned but contextless — fail-closed direction and self-heals on next restart, but document/handle the intermediate state deliberately. Design revocation carefully against IID-collision trust-replacement protections; add tests for config-removal revocation and restart-after-partial-install.
